messages:
maya: CI alerts for the Llama 3 13B mixed-precision rollout — getting OOMs on ded-2 when batch_size > 8. Any ideas?
eli: I saw the same on a couple of nodes. Only happens with the mixed int8+fp16 path. fp16-only is fine.
sam: can you paste the minimal error or stack?
maya: sure, here's the top of the worker log: 
```
RuntimeError: CUDA out of memory. Tried to allocate 512.00 MiB (GPU 0; 48.00 GiB total, 41.20 GiB already allocated)
  File "/srv/runtime/runner.py", line 342, in forward
    outputs = kernel_dispatch(model, inputs)
  File "/srv/runtime/kernels/selector.py", line 128, in kernel_dispatch
    return fallback_gemm(x, w)
```

perf-bot: profiling snapshot uploaded: https://perf.internal/runs/2034567890 (summary: kernel switch -> fallback, peak mem +20%) :chart_with_upwards_trend:
nish: quick theory — the mixed-precision kernel selector seems to fall back to the generic GEMM for some head sizes when quantized packing is in play. If fallback uses full-FP32 accumulation paths we can blow memory. Also saw odd KV cache dtype casts in trace.
chris: could tokenization/chat template differences be changing sequence lengths or padding and triggering larger KV buffers?
maya: possible — recent chat template tweak adds system prompt + conversation history trimming which changed prefix lengths from avg 48 -> 120 tokens. Repro command below: 
```
./run_infer --model llama3-13b --precision mixed --batch 12 --prompt-file tests/long-prefixs.txt --profile
```

eli: replicated locally with that script. NVTX shows kernel selector deciding: quantized-kernel for heads=16, but for head_dim=64 it falls back. The fallback gemm is using float32 accumulation. Memory spike lines up with KV alloc at 3rd token step.
sam: short-term mitigation: cap auto-batch size for mixed precision and enforce per-request max_tokens to 1024. Also we should avoid combining prefix-heavy chat templates with mixed precision until we fix selector heuristics.
nish: I dug into selector heuristics — we're using heuristics that assume stable head_dim distribution. Newer llama3 configs with non-power-of-two head dims break the packing algorithm, causing an alignment failure and selector to pick the generic path. We should add an explicit kernel-support matrix keyed by (model_name, head_dim, dtype_profile) to avoid heuristic misfires.
chris: can we add a guard to keep KV cache dtype consistent (don't cast per-token) — that might avoid the per-step spike?
maya: tried a quick patch that forces KV cache to the tensor dtype of the model; mem usage reduced by ~30% in a dev run. Will open PR.
perf-bot: flamegraph: main peak at token 3  — kernel_fallback_gemm (60%), kv_alloc (25%), cuda_memcpy (10%). link: https://perf.internal/graphs/2034567890/fg
eli: good catch. For rollout plan: 1) revert mixed-precision canary for L3-13B on ded-2; 2) add temporary batching cap in config; 3) engineer selector matrix and KV dtype guard; 4) re-run perf tests with long-prefix chat templates.
sam: I'll add the batching cap and canary rollback to the release plan.
nish: I'll start the selector matrix PR and add unit tests for head_dim edge cases.
maya: thanks — assigning tasks in the thread: @sam (batching cap + rollback), @nish (selector matrix + tests), @eli (re-run perf harness with new prefix distribution), @chris (validate KV dtype guard on multi-gpu).
chris: ack.
maya: also leaving a note: we should add a test case in the chat-template regression suite that simulates longer system prompts so we don't regress silently.
eli: +1.
sam: rolling back the canary now. I'll post update when it's done. :thumbsup: 
perf-bot: deploy rollback triggered by @sam at 2034568002.
maya: good, thanks everyone. We'll reconvene after PRs land and reprofile.
